text:
jordan-ops: heads up — us-west2 just lost two racks (maintenance + failed drain) and we're seeing a ~45% drop in available GPU slots. lots of tiny pods pending and a wave of evictions. autoscaler logs show quota rejections. anyone else observing this spike?

ana-eng: seeing it from the app side — latency up on batch inference and a ton of OOMKilled sidecars, small-gang jobs stuck Pending. dashboard shows node taints from maintenance, but a bunch of nodes still schedulable with free slots. weird packing behavior.

lee-platform: confirmed: scheduler is refusing to binpack small pods onto remaining nodes because of an anti-affinity rule we rolled out last week (podTopologySpread + requiredDuringScheduling). it used to be preferred, not required. that rollout might be the trigger.

matt-sre: autoscaler hit per-AZ instance quota; cloud console shows no additional nodes allowed. i'll request quota bump but that's not instant. short term we can relax the topology constraint via a feature flag or admit small pods as best-effort.

sophia-infra: +1. we also have a nodeSelector on some jobs forcing gpu-type=a100 and those nodes are the ones drained. a quick mitigation is to toggle the nodeSelector for lower-priority queues to allow packing onto v100 pool.

jordan-ops: can we do a fast patch? steps I propose: 1) temporarily change the podTopologySpread to preferred for tiny-gang class, 2) allow best-effort placement onto v100 via label override, 3) bump warm-pool target if quota allows. who can run the patch?

ana-eng: I can submit a PR to the deploy config to flip the spread rule for pods with label workload=tiny-gang. it's low risk. snippet: ```yaml
spec:
  topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
    whenUnsatisfiable: PreferDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution
```

lee-platform: thanks. also suggest a short-lived scheduler tweak: relax preemption holdoff for tiny pods so they can be squeezed between larger running jobs. add this to the scheduler config with a 10m TTL.

matt-sre: pushed a ticket to cloud to raise us-west2 GPU quota (case #10238) but ETA ~2-6 hrs. For immediate relief, I've manually increased warm-pool target on the a100 pool by +4 (if cloud allows). autoscale-bot: shows 0/4 launched due to quota, so still blocked.

autoscale-bot: warning: instance launch failed: QuotaExceeded.GPUs. Region=us-west2. Requested=4, Available=0.

sophia-infra: ok while quota is pending, let's prioritize changes that avoid evictions: 1) flip spread rule (ana PR), 2) relax nodeSelector for non-urgent jobs (i'll coordinate with the teams), 3) add an eviction grace tweak to increase eviction threshold CPU/memory by 10% for 1h.

jordan-ops: can someone run the following k8s command to patch the default scheduler policy quickly? ```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap scheduler-config --patch '{"data":{"policy":"relaxTinyPodPreemption: true"}}'``` this is a temporary toggle — revert after quota restored.

lee-platform: i'll run the patch and watch scheduler-e2e. doing it now.

lee-platform: patched. monitoring binpacking metrics — tiny-pod pending count dropping slowly. will keep an eye on eviction rate.

ana-eng: PR merged to flip spread to preferred for workload=tiny-gang. rolling out now.

matt-sre: cloud quota bumped (provisional) — autoscaler started 2 nodes into us-west2. capacity gap closing.

jordan-ops: great — after this stabilizes let's plan a postmortem: root cause is combination of (a) required topology constraint rollout, (b) simultaneous maintenance on a100 racks, (c) hard per-AZ quota. action items: revert risky rollouts to preferredByDefault gating, add quota-runbook for emergency requests, and improve autoscaler visibility for quota failures. I'll create the doc. :spiral_calendar:

sophia-infra: agree. also propose an autoscaler feature: if quota==0, temporarily allow cross-AZ placement (if app permits) or enable spill-to-different-GPU-type with quantization hints. we'll scope next sprint.

jordan-ops: thanks all. keeping this thread open until metrics are back to normal.
